description:
Rather than committing the Double Choc to a single category, we designed it as a platform with range.

With adjustable suspension configurations, the bike can be built from a capable trail setup to a more aggressive all‑mountain configuration. Running 140/136 mm gives a balanced, efficient trail bike that pedals willingly and stays composed on long rides. Pushing it to 160/148 mm shifts the focus toward steeper, rougher terrain while retaining control and predictability.

This versatility isn’t about indecision – it’s about acknowledging that riding styles, terrain and priorities change. The frame supports those choices without losing its character.

The Double Choc combines a steel front triangle with an aluminum rear end, because each material contributes differently to how the bike behaves.

Steel up front adds durability and a ride feel that remains calm over sustained rough terrain. It provides subtle feedback rather than filtering everything out – something that matters on long days and repeated impacts. The aluminum rear triangle brings stiffness and precision where suspension performance and tracking are critical, keeping the bike sharp when loading the rear end through berms and compressions. Together, the materials form a system that feels controlled rather than overbuilt.

The Double Choc uses a Horst‑link four‑bar suspension design. This layout allows pedaling forces, braking behavior and bump absorption to be tuned independently.

The result is a suspension platform that remains efficient under power while staying active over uneven terrain. Anti‑squat characteristics support climbing and acceleration, while anti‑rise behavior keeps the bike stable under braking on steep descents. Instead of feeling isolated from the trail, the suspension encourages momentum and consistency.

We chose commonly available bearings, hardware and threads to keep long‑term maintenance straightforward. Serviceability isn’t a secondary concern here – it’s part of the design brief.

The geometry of the Double Choc is progressive, but measured.

It’s built to reward commitment rather than constant correction. Stable at speed, predictable when pushed hard and balanced when terrain gets steep or loose. The bike invites big moves, but keeps enough composure to stay manageable when fatigue sets in.

Rather than chasing numbers for their own sake, the geometry reflects how the bike is actually ridden: hard descents followed by real climbs, repeated over long days.

The Double Choc is the result of several years of development.

From early ideas to multiple prototypes, the platform matured through riding, testing and refinement. Changes were introduced when they added clarity – not novelty. The result is a bike that feels settled, not experimental.

This development process shaped a frame that encourages confidence rather than demanding it.

Every Double Choc frame is built by hand in our workshop in Saxony.

Designing and building under the same roof keeps decisions grounded. Tube selection, gussets, reinforcements and alignment are considered as part of the complete structure, not as afterthoughts. The frame is built to tolerate repeated hard use, not just perfect conditions.

This is a bike intended to be ridden often and pushed hard.

The Double Choc is for riders who want to go further into terrain, ride bigger lines and still pedal back out with control.

It’s not about owning multiple bikes for different moods. It’s about having one bike that makes sense across a wide range of riding – because it was designed that way from the start.

At Sour, steel is not a stylistic choice.It’s a design decision.

We use steel because it allows us to define frame behavior precisely — under load, over time, and across a wide range of riding conditions. Material choice, tube selection and heat treatment directly influence how a frame transfers forces, responds to repeated stress and ages through use.

Our manufacturing represents the culmination of plans, chats with friends while out riding, and many late nights writing ideas down. Our on-shoring process, the project we started to make all our frames right here in Germany, one-by-one, by hand, in our own facilities is our biggest adventure yet.

It is by far the biggest step we’ve ever made as a company: moving 100% of our production to Saxony. We are so proud to be Made in Germany and will continue to grow the project in the coming years.

Sour Bicycles 4130 CrMo frame welded by hand in Saxony, featuring heat treated, multi-butted tubing.

The bottom bracket is a custom part designed by Sour and fits a standard 73mm BSA threaded bottom bracket. The headtube is also a Sour-specific design.

The rear triangle is 7075 T6 aluminum and is made by Actofive in Dresden. SRAM UDH derailleur hanger and Transmission-ready.

The seat clamp is designed in-house and is integrated into the frame. Should it ever fail, the frame can be professionally modified to use a traditional clamp, if repair of the original clamp is not possible. We have never seen one fail.

We’ve tried to make all the details of the Double Choc as straight forward as possible so know you what you’re getting into. Still not sure? Just drop us an email!

Below is the sample weight of a size medium Double Choc. This weight does not include powdercoating, but please keep in mind that your chose powdercoat may be heavier than the average coating we use. Fades, gradients, and metallic colours can weigh more than single solid colour. If you are interested the final weight, please get in touch. We apply an inside wax coating before shipping the frame to your door that will add additional weight.

A Sour Double Choc frameset weighs 3.8 kg in size medium with all it’s small parts and suspension pivots, bearings, and bolts installed. This weight is excluding powdercoat which will add between 50g and 200g depending on your color choice.

Included with your Double Choc frame or frameset are all small parts, cable guides and bolts to build your bike. You get a rear thru-axle of course, and if you’re ordering a frameset, you get a front axle with your fork as well. Headsets are only included if you add one to your order.

We are currently working on more options for the Cowboy Cookie, but currently we offer some amazing options from Fox and Manitou that work perfectly with our suspension design. If you have any questions about tuning or clearance, feel free to drop us an email.

You can add a rear shock and other parts at check out.
